messages:
kai.sales: Quick alert  POC with Meridian Inc — they report lots of events in the console with trace_id=null. Their forwarder logs show a short window of 403s followed by 429s, and their security team just pinged us with a data-residency question.
fran.ops: Can you paste the forwarder log snippet + sample event? Also forward the security Qs separately.
kai.sales: Logs and sample event below (sanitized):
```
2026-12-01T02:14:10Z INFO forwarder batch=9 size=1.9MB start_upload
2026-12-01T02:14:11Z ERROR upload status=403 err="SASExpired" attempt=0
2026-12-01T02:14:11Z INFO refreshing sas_token ttl=300
2026-12-01T02:14:12Z WARN partial_upload committed_metadata but payload missing
2026-12-01T02:14:14Z ERROR upload status=429 err="IngestThrottled" attempt=1
```
sample event: `{ "ts":"2026-12-01T02:14:10Z", "msg":"user.signup", "trace_id":null }`
```
noah.eng: Interesting  Azure SAS expiry + ingest throttle. Slightly different root than STS but same symptom: metadata (trace mapping) persisted for a slice while payload objects failed/retried -> joiner drops trace_id.
anya-support: One-line for their SREs?
kai.sales: "Signed/SAS token expired mid-batch causing partial metadata commits; increase SAS TTL or issue per-object SAS immediately before upload. Short-term: enable atomic/local buffering or reduce batch size."
fran.ops: Security Qs: Meridian asked whether buffering writes any PII to local disk and if local buffers are encrypted. I replied: "Forwarder local buffering writes encrypted files to local disk, controlled by `forwarder.local_encryption=true` and follows customer KMS when using our upload-proxy." Can we confirm?
noah.eng: Correct. Local buffering uses AES-256 with a per-instance key wrapped by customer KMS when using the upload-proxy; we should share a short QA line.
sec-qa-bot: [sec-qa] Meridian security questionnaire item 7: data residency and disk encryption answered by infra-team.
fran.ops: Also they asked about cost impact of the temporary ingest burst.
quota-bot: [quota] Temporary ingest burst granted org=meridian-55 ttl=3h by noah.eng :white_check_mark:
kai.sales: Thanks. Include a short billing note for Meridian: bursts are transient and appear as usage; we can show estimated token/ingest cost before applying.
noah.eng: Config snippet to give them (YAML):
```
forwarder:
  buffer_mode: atomic
  local_encryption: true
  azure_sas_ttl_seconds: 1200
  max_batch_size_mb: 1.0
  retry:
    max_attempts: 4
```
fran.ops: If they can't modify SAS TTL they can rotate per-object SAS on-demand or route uploads through our KMS-backed proxy (ent-only). Both options avoid mid-batch expiry.
anya-support: They also asked whether missing trace_ids mean data lost. Short answer?
kai.sales: "Most data is retried; however when metadata commits without payloads we cannot reconstruct trace mapping for those events. Best fix: atomic buffering or per-object SAS so metadata and payload commit together."
noah.eng: Follow-ups: 1) ops to run a dedup/consistency check after buffering enabled 2) eng to add a console banner when >0.5% of recent batches have missing trace_id due to upload errors 3) sales to attach the security QA snippet and the billing note to the POC report.
fran.ops: Running dedup/consistency scan now; will report in ~30m.
quota-bot: [reminder] ingest burst meridian-55 expires in 2h 45m  will post 15m before expiry.
anya-support: I'll send the YAML, one-liner, security QA lines, and cost note to Meridian SRE and sec team. Marking this thread for follow-up. :thumbsup:
